submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad previous-token head: predict ordinary English text of five or more words ACTIVE, weakly (about 0.25-0.5 of max) on some ordinary noun or verb, whether or not it contains a trigger, and strongly active (0.55-1.0 of max) on the word right after 'how'/'How' when that word is the degree adjective/adverb/quantifier it modifies ('how much/big/secure/protected/glad'), and somewhat less (about 0.5-0.7) on the noun after 'both' ('both sides'), 'of' in 'what kind of', and the verb after 'To'/'to' or 'When' ('To achieve', 'When evaluating'). The only inactive classes are a single-token word or interjection with punctuation ('Yes.', 'Hello.', 'Right?', 'Stop!') and bare decimals, percentages, prices and fractions ('3.14159', '98.6', '3.5%', '$1,299.00', '1/2'); short sentences of three or four words and non-English text sit near the line and are not part of the claim.

rival_explanations: Narrow reading: only the word modified by 'how' is strongly active and 'both'/'what kind'/'to'/'when' pairs are no stronger than ordinary prose, so 'Both sides agreed.' or 'To achieve this, we worked.' would peak at the prose level.

Broader reading: the head is strong on any word that strongly attends to a preceding function word (determiner, preposition, conjunction), so 'the sides', 'on Monday' or 'and protect' would be as strong as 'both sides' and 'how secure'.
